GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production code with no tests, fewer than 8 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these — create both):
  server/pipeline/episode_dag.py
  tests/test_episode_dag.py

WHY THIS EXISTS, from a real failure today. The repo contained
server/pipeline/guest_email_context.py, fully working: one call returned the guest's emailed
headshot ("prof headshot minimized.webp") and his real links (his website, his own podcast).
NOTHING IN THE PIPELINE EVER CALLED IT. The episode published with a thumbnail that did not
use the guest's face and show notes carrying only a CRM-scraped LinkedIn URL, while his
material sat unread. generate_thumbnail already accepted a guest_photo_path parameter; it was
simply never given one.

The defect class is not a missing feature. It is a step that exists, is never invoked, and
whose absence produces NO signal. The owner's instruction: model the process as a DAG so
steps cannot be silently skipped.

BUILD server/pipeline/episode_dag.py — pure, stdlib only, no IO of its own:

  A STEP is declared with: id, requires (tuple of step ids), produces (tuple of artifact
  keys), optional (bool, default False), and a description.

  EPISODE_DAG: the declared graph for an episode, covering at least: assets_downloaded,
  stems_built, transcript, content_edit, angle_render, audio_master, final_render,
  certification, guest_assets (the step that was skipped), show_notes, clips, thumbnail,
  publish_expectation, publish, promo_email, promo_schedule.
  guest_assets must be declared as a REQUIREMENT of both thumbnail and show_notes, because
  that is the dependency whose absence caused the incident. Encode the real relationships;
  read the modules in the worktree to get them right rather than guessing.

  validate_dag(dag) -> list[str]
      Structural problems: unknown requirement ids, cycles, a step producing an artifact
      another step also produces, unreachable steps. Empty list means the graph is sound.
      This runs in tests so a malformed graph cannot ship.

  topological_order(dag) -> list[str]
      Deterministic order. Raises on a cycle rather than returning a partial order.

  plan_next(dag, completed, *, available_artifacts=()) -> list[dict]
      Steps whose requirements are all satisfied and which are not yet completed, in
      topological order, each {"id","reason","blocked_by"}.

  audit_run(dag, completed, *, produced_artifacts) -> dict
      THE HEART OF THIS MODULE. Returns
        {"complete": bool, "skipped": [...], "missing_artifacts": [...], "report": str}
      A step is SKIPPED when a downstream step completed but this step did not, even though
      it was required. That is exactly the guest_assets case: thumbnail completed while
      guest_assets never ran. An optional step that did not run is reported as "skipped
      (optional)" and does NOT make complete False, but it is still NAMED, because silence
      is what let the incident happen.
      The report string must be human-readable and must name every skipped step and the
      downstream step that ran without it.

  Determinism throughout: same inputs, same output and same ordering.

TESTS (tests/test_episode_dag.py; at least 8):
 (1) validate_dag(EPISODE_DAG) returns an empty list — the shipped graph is sound;
 (2) topological_order respects every declared requirement;
 (3) NEGATIVE and central, THE REAL INCIDENT: completed includes thumbnail and show_notes
     but NOT guest_assets; audit_run reports guest_assets as skipped and names thumbnail
     and show_notes as the downstream steps that ran without it, and complete is False;
 (4) NEGATIVE: a cycle raises from topological_order and is reported by validate_dag;
 (5) NEGATIVE: an unknown requirement id is reported by validate_dag;
 (6) plan_next returns only steps whose requirements are met, in topological order;
 (7) an optional step that did not run is NAMED in the report but does not set complete
     False;
 (8) determinism: two identical calls produce identical output including order;
 (9) guest_assets is declared as a requirement of BOTH thumbnail and show_notes — assert
     this directly, so a future edit that drops it fails the suite.
tasks.verified: the episode declared as a dependency graph, with an audit that names any step a downstream step ran without

THE DEFECT, hit on a real episode today. validate_show_notes runs content_mechanics over the
show notes, including the QUOTES section. It reported:
    quotes.items[0].text: mechanics CONTRACTIONS: Contraction rate is 0.000;
    add natural contractions to reach at least 0.004.
That quote is a VERBATIM transcription of what the guest said, carrying a speaker and a
timestamp. Style rules about how Ankit writes cannot be applied to another person's recorded
words. Following that instruction would mean EDITING A QUOTE to add contractions the speaker
did not say, which is fabrication of the exact kind the timestamp-and-speaker requirement
exists to prevent.

THE FIX — mechanics must know the difference between authored prose and quoted speech:
1. Add a concept of VERBATIM content to check_mechanics: a caller can mark an item as
   verbatim (e.g. an item field "verbatim": True). Verbatim items are EXEMPT from the
   style rules that only make sense for authored copy: CONTRACTIONS, BANNED_TERMS,
   SENTENCE_LENGTH, and the self-answered-question rule.
2. Verbatim items remain SUBJECT TO checks that are about integrity rather than style: they
   still count toward CROSS_ITEM_REUSE (the same quote must not be pasted into three posts)
   and they must still be non-empty. Document which rules apply and which do not, and why,
   in the module docstring.
3. In show_notes_structure.validate_show_notes, mark quote items as verbatim when handing
   them to check_mechanics. Do not exempt the hook, guest_intro, about_guest or any other
   authored field.
4. A banned term or a run-on appearing inside a verbatim quote must be reported as ADVISORY
   (visible, not blocking), so a human can decide to trim the quote or pick a different one.
   It must never be reported as something to rewrite.

TESTS (tests/test_verbatim_exemption.py; at least 5):
 (1) THE REAL CASE: a quote with zero contractions marked verbatim produces NO blocking
     contraction violation;
 (2) NEGATIVE: the same text NOT marked verbatim still produces the contraction violation —
     the exemption must be opt-in, never the default;
 (3) NEGATIVE: authored fields in show notes (the hook) are still checked; inject a 42-word
     hook and assert it still fails;
 (4) a banned term inside a verbatim quote is reported as advisory rather than blocking;
 (5) NEGATIVE: the same quote text appearing in two items still trips CROSS_ITEM_REUSE even
     when both are verbatim — integrity rules survive the exemption;
 (6) validate_show_notes on a realistic set with quotes lacking contractions returns no
     blocking problem for those quotes.
Keep the existing mechanics and show-notes suites green.
